cards.text: Five Amorite kings went to war against Gibeon, and the LORD gave them over to Israel (Joshua 10:5, 12). Now those five kings have fled and hidden together. FIVE kings, ONE hiding spot, and I bet ZERO elbow room.

cards.question: Where are the five kings hiding?

cards.text: Then word reaches Joshua, Israel's leader: the five kings have been found. Hide and seek is OVER, fellas.

cards.question: With the five kings found, what does Joshua tell his men to do to the cave?

answers.text: Roll large stones against its mouth
Dig a trench around its entrance
Light a fire at its entrance

cards.text: He posts men there to guard them too, so five kings are stuck in the dark behind a wall of stones. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I wouldn't trade places with them.

cards.question: With the kings shut in behind the stones, what does Joshua tell the rest of his men to do?

answers.text: Chase the enemy and attack from behind
Head back to camp and rest up
Gather the spoils from the field

cards.question: Joshua tells his men not to let the enemy reach their ___, because the LORD has delivered them into their hand.

cards.text: So Israel keeps up the attack until they've finished off the enemy armies. The survivors who are left retreat to their fortified cities.

cards.question: After the chase, Israel's army comes back to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah with many men lost.
Once the army is back, the text says no one dares to say a word against the Israelites.

cards.text: Then Joshua says, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me." Out they come: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

cards.question: Joshua gathers all the men of Israel. Then he tells the ___ who came with him to put their feet on the necks of these kings.

cards.text: Then Joshua says not to be afraid or discouraged, but to be strong and courageous. And he gives a reason.

cards.question: Why does Joshua say there's no need to be afraid?

answers.text: The LORD will do this to all their enemies
The rest of the kings have already given up
Their army is bigger than any in the land

cards.text: After this, Joshua strikes down the five kings and hangs their bodies on five trees.

cards.question: Joshua leaves the kings' bodies hanging on the trees through the night.
At sunset the bodies are thrown into the cave where the kings hid, and large stones are placed at its mouth. What does the text say about those stones?

answers.text: They were still there when this was written
They were rolled away a few years later
They were carried off to build an altar

cards.text: On that same day, Joshua captures Makkedah, the town with the cave, and then he moves with all Israel from city to city: Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir. At each one, Joshua captures the city and leaves no survivors, just as he had done before. When Horam king of Gezer comes to help Lachish, Joshua strikes him down along with his people.

So Joshua conquers the whole region: the hill country, the Negev, the foothills and the slopes, together with all their kings. It stretches from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

cards.question: Joshua devoted to destruction everything that breathed. The text says he did it just as who had commanded?

answers.text: The LORD the God of Israel

cards.question: Joshua needs several campaigns to capture all these kings and their land.
Why is Joshua able to capture all these kings and their land?

answers.text: Because the LORD fought for Israel
Because the kings had no city walls

cards.question: When it's all done, Joshua returns with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
